I talk a lot with passengers, sometimes I catch myself going on and on and they look uncomfortable, but it’s like I can’t hit the brakes.

Lately, I also get this feeling that people on the street or in the back seat are somehow paying extra attention to me, like they’re judging or talking about me, even when I can’t really hear what they’re saying. D001-D005_h020.question:
I’ve been struggling at work for maybe the past year or so, but it’s gotten a lot more noticeable over the last several months. I’m an air traffic controller, so details really matter, and lately I keep overlooking small things on the screen—like misreading a callsign or missing a minor change—stuff I never used to miss. I also keep misplacing my headset, notes, even my badge, and I waste time hunting for them.

My mind feels pulled in ten directions. I get distracted by background chatter in the tower or even by my own thoughts in the middle of a handoff. It’s like I’m half a step behind. When I’m off duty, I can’t seem to relax; I feel keyed up, restless, pacing around the house, flipping between TV, my phone, and half-started projects. Even sitting through a movie with my wife, I’m fidgeting or checking my phone.

I get irritated if I have to wait in lines or let others go first; I feel this urge to cut ahead or rush things. On top of that, every now and then I’m convinced I hear someone say my name or see something out of the corner of my eye, but when I look, no one’s there. It makes me doubt my own concentration even more.
D001-D005_h020.options:
A. Anorexia Nervosa
    B. Schizophrenia
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D001-D005_h020.answer: C & B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h021.question:
I guess the main thing is I feel like my brain just won’t cooperate with me anymore. At work, I’m constantly missing little things in the code or in client emails—typos, wrong file versions, overlooking a line that breaks the whole build. It’s not that I don’t know how to do it; it’s like my attention just slips, and I only notice when something goes wrong.  

People give me instructions—my project manager, or even my ex when it was about co‑parenting schedules—and I’ll start, then my mind drifts or I get sidetracked, and suddenly I realize I never finished what I was supposed to do. That’s been happening more in the last year or so, at least that’s when I really started noticing it.  

I have a hard time sitting still. On calls I’m pacing around the apartment, fidgeting, checking other tabs. I feel like I’m always buzzing, like I can’t switch off. I also cut people off a lot in meetings, jump into conversations before they’re done, and only realize afterward that I’ve talked over them.  

On top of that, every now and then I get these moments where I’m not sure if what I’m noticing—like faint voices or shadows at the edge of my vision—is actually there or just in my head. It doesn’t happen constantly, but it’s unsettling enough that it’s making me question my grip on things.
D001-D005_h021.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h021.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h022.question:
It’s hard to piece together when this all really started, but over the last several months it’s become a lot more obvious to me and my husband. I keep messing things up in little ways. I’ll be helping my daughter with her homework and I’ll skip parts of the directions or misread them, and then realize later I’d led her totally wrong. I burn food all the time because I think I’ve set the timer, then get distracted and just… lose track. Even simple things, like paying a bill or filling out a school form, I’ll miss a line or write something in the wrong place.

My husband will ask me to do three or four things before he leaves for work—call the pediatrician, switch the laundry, send an email—and by the afternoon I’ve half‑done one and completely forgotten the others. It’s like I start tasks and then they just disappear from my brain.

I can’t sit still; I’m constantly pacing, fiddling with something, jumping up from the table. The kids joke that I move faster than they do, but it doesn’t feel funny. I talk over people without meaning to, cut into my kids’ conversations, finish my husband’s sentences, and he gets annoyed.

What’s scaring me most lately, though, are these moments where I hear someone say my name or a comment, clear as day, and no one’s actually spoken. Sometimes I catch something out of the corner of my eye—like a shadow or someone standing there—and when I look, nothing’s there. It makes me second‑guess myself, like I don’t fully trust my own senses anymore.
D001-D005_h022.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h022.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h023.question:
I’ve been struggling at work for maybe… a year? Hard to pin down exactly. I keep messing up basic things I should be good at. I’ll pour a flight and realize I skipped one glass, or I’ll mix up vintages even when the bottles are right in front of me. I’ll read the tasting notes before service and then somehow miss small but important details, like the grape blend or region, and my manager has to correct me.

People give me instructions and I start, but I drift off or get sidetracked. My boss will ask me to reset the tasting bar and run a stock check; I’ll wipe a few counters, then get pulled into something else and never finish. At home, it’s the same with chores—I start laundry, then find it still in the machine the next day.

I feel like I’m constantly in motion, pacing between the cellar and the bar, rearranging things that don’t really need it. Coworkers tease me that I can’t stand still; it feels like there’s this motor in me that doesn’t shut off. I also cut people off a lot—guests, colleagues—jumping into their sentences or finishing their thoughts before they’re done. I see their faces tighten, but it’s like I’ve already spoken before I realize I should have waited.
D001-D005_h023.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h023.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h024.question:
I’ve been struggling quite a bit at work the past few months. On site, I’ll be halfway through laying out a garden bed and suddenly realize I’ve planted the wrong shrubs in the wrong pattern, or I’ve measured something totally off. It’s not that I don’t know how to do it; it’s like my mind drifts and I miss obvious things, then have to redo them.

My boss will give me a list for the day, and I’ll start strong, but then I jump to another task before I’ve finished the first. By the end of the day there are half-done jobs all over the place. At home it’s similar: I’ll start cleaning, then wander off and never finish.

I also feel like I can’t sit still. Even on breaks, I’m pacing around, fiddling with tools, getting up and down. People joke that I’m always buzzing, but it doesn’t feel funny to me; it’s exhausting.

I catch myself talking over coworkers, cutting into their conversations or decisions on site without meaning to. Sometimes I feel like I’m reacting to things around me that others don’t really notice, which makes me even more jumpy and distracted.
D001-D005_h024.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h024.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia

D001-D005_h025.question:
I’ve been struggling for…honestly, I’m not even sure how long now, a few years at least. My wife keeps pointing out that I miss obvious things. I’ll sign off on a contract and later someone in finance finds a stupid mistake I should have caught in the first read-through. It’s not that I don’t know how to do my job; my mind just slips over details, like my eyes are moving faster than my brain.

It’s similar with follow-through. I’ll tell my team we’re going to push a new initiative, I start strong, then it sort of fizzles. Emails go unanswered, tasks half-done. At home, my wife jokes not to give me more than one chore at a time, because I’ll wander off and never finish.

I feel like I’m constantly in motion. Even in board meetings, I’m bouncing my leg, checking my phone, getting up to refill water. People say I pace when I’m on calls. I also cut people off a lot—finish their sentences, jump into conversations before they’re done. It’s gotten worse lately.

On top of that, every now and then, I get these odd experiences—like hearing someone say my name when no one’s there, or being sure people are talking about me at work, even though I can’t prove it. It’s unsettling enough that I’m starting to doubt my own judgment.
D001-D005_h025.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation)
    C. Specific Phobia
    D. Binge-Eating Disorder
D001-D005_h025.answer: B & A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Combined Presentation) & Schizophrenia
